# GTDB-TK Classify {#sec-classify}

## Introduction

In september, when I was still inexperienced, I ran GTDB-Tk on the 10 samples using the `classify_wf`. At the time, that is the only way I thought it could be used. I got a few trees output from this, but because the trees were not monophyletic, so I discarded them as not possible to be correct. However, there was another output that I did not see or disregarded.

## Methods

The script used was the same as in the de_novo process.

## Results

### Table

The table was too large to include here, so here is a link to it in the repo: [gtdbtk.bac120.summary.tsv](https://github.com/tobiasnunn/tnunn_research/blob/6bfc481b8ebb4b2d3d0ec013bfe68a3662fb4ca4/Research_Experience_Module/02_middle-analysis_outputs/gtdbtk_stuff/classify_wf/gtdbtk.bac120.summary.tsv)

### tree example

```{r}
#| echo: FALSE
#| label: fig-badtree
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-cap: "Early phylogenetic tree made using the GTDB-Tk classify workflow"

knitr::include_graphics(here::here("img/classify/classify_tree.png"))
```

@fig-badtree shows that the clade is not monophyletic, with representatives from 3 genera (*Enterobacter, Erwinia* and *Pantoea*).

## Manual trees

At some point I made a set of trees that cannot be sourced to any other analysis I performed at the time.

These were made using [This script](https://github.com/aptemus/tnunn_research/blob/0c487ca21d0c783b7075446d688f88ed1d7ce77a/2024-25%20Research/frog%20bacteria/03%20data_analysis/call%20API%20and%20process%20json%20-%20with%20legend.R), which does not exist in the current version of the repo. I cannot find what process made the basis of these trees. I remember, as well as the small trees it output a big tree of everything that did have them in the right place, which I also found bizarre, so I did some manual pruning in Dendroscope (I could not do it in R yet). That produced these trees:

### Sphingomonas samples

```{r}
#| echo: FALSE
#| label: fig-S
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-cap: "Phylogenetic tree for 4 local samples of the genus *Sphingomonas*"

knitr::include_graphics(here::here("img/other_trees/sphingomona.png"))
```

1Dt100g - Odd sample, very distant to everything else, no species name means we don’t know if that is correct, but it is still in the right genus at least 3Dt1c - No species, matched up with another without species ID, so likely the same but unhelpful for our purposes 3Dt2c - Matched with a speciesless sample, there are an odd number of those in this tree, maybe something to look into, so it might be correct, there are no other samples on the tree under “panni”, maybe should check NIH for “Sphingomonas panni” as if there is one and it isn’t on the tree, our one could be miscategorized 3Dt2j - Good sample, sister to a reference sample of the same species

### 1Dt1h

```{r}
#| echo: FALSE
#| label: fig-11h
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-cap: "Early phylogenetic tree made using the GTDB-Tk classify workflow"

knitr::include_graphics(here::here("img/other_trees/1Dt1h_orig.png"))
```

1Dt1h - Far away from all other groups on its own and in the wrong genus cluster, it’s a “Microbacterium” surrounded by “Brevibacterium” so very likely wrong.

### 1Dt2d

```{r}
#| echo: FALSE
#| label: fig-12d
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-cap: "Early phylogenetic tree made using the GTDB-Tk classify workflow"

knitr::include_graphics(here::here("img/other_trees/1Dt2d.png"))
```

1Dt2d - Likely correct classification as the sister sample is of the same species, however it is not a reference so confidence is lower.

### 2Dt1l

```{r}
#| echo: FALSE
#| label: fig-21l
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-cap: "Early phylogenetic tree made using the GTDB-Tk classify workflow"

knitr::include_graphics(here::here("img/other_trees/2Dt1l_orig.png"))
```

2Dt1l - Warning alarms on this one, it is a “Brevibacterium”, surrounded by “Microbacterium”, so very likely miscategorized somewhere.

### 3Dt2h

```{r}
#| echo: FALSE
#| label: fig-32h
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-cap: "Early phylogenetic tree made using the GTDB-Tk classify workflow"

knitr::include_graphics(here::here("img/other_trees/3Dt2h.png"))
```

3Dt2h - This is an odd one, it isn’t matched with a “microbacterium testaceum”, but the one it is matched has no species ID so it could be, the weird thing is there are “testaceum” samples all over the tree that aren’t next to each other, but they are all “microbacterium” so ID is probably accurate.

### Other two samples

```{r}
#| echo: FALSE
#| label: fig-O2
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-cap: "Early phylogenetic tree made using the GTDB-Tk classify workflow"

knitr::include_graphics(here::here("img/other_trees/Other_two.png"))
```

1Dt100h - Sister to the entire rest of the tree, so quite distinct, but the “closest” reference is of the same genus, this is another without species ID, so it could loosely be the same, I think its enough to confirm genus anyway. This is the sample that all other analyses could not even work out the family of.

All of these trees use the names originally given to them by Alberto from his blastn analysis. (thats what the notebook said he did to get those names)

I did an analysis table in Notebook 1.

I noted that it seems samples 1Dt2d and 2Dt1l looked flipped, so I changed the names and the trees started making more sense:

```{r}
#| echo: FALSE
#| label: fig-11hf
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-cap: "Early phylogenetic tree made using the GTDB-Tk classify workflow"

knitr::include_graphics(here::here("img/other_trees/1Dt1h_fix.png"))
```

```{r}
#| echo: FALSE
#| label: fig-21lf
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-cap: "Early phylogenetic tree made using the GTDB-Tk classify workflow"

knitr::include_graphics(here::here("img/other_trees/2Dt1l_fixed.png"))
```

This seems to have fixed the issues. Due to these being created early on, they do not have good dimensions for presentation, this is something I fix in @sec-denovo.
